svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 2. Four things that defeat a burner phone, and what one is actually for
svg.desc: Four defeat mechanisms. First, more than 155 countries now require identity documents to register a prepaid subscriber module, so an unregistered one is not purchasable in most of the world. Second, the purchase itself is recorded by cameras and timestamps even when paid in cash. Third, and most important, a second device that travels the same routes at the same times as your usual one is linked by pattern rather than by name, and research finds that most pairs of people who call each other have shared a tower. Fourth, a single moment of carelessness such as one power-on at home undoes everything. A band below states what a burner is actually good for, and what it is not.
svg.text: The usual instructions are cash purchase, never power it on near your real phone, destroy it afterwards. All true, and all insufficient.

svg.text: What a second device is genuinely good for, which is not what the guidance implies

g.text: Compartmentalisation. A device that holds client work and nothing else, so a personal compromise is not a client compromise. This works, it is boring, and it is the actual use.
Travel with reduced exposure. A device carrying nothing sensitive across a border, so a search finds nothing. Figure 3. This also works.
A clean device for an untrusted environment. Conference networks, client sites, anywhere you would rather not connect your real phone.

svg.text: What it is not good for, and where the usual guidance becomes actively unsafe
Genuine anonymity against a capable investigator. Not because the technique is wrong, but because it has to be executed perfectly, over a long period, by somebody
who has never done it before, in a country whose subscriber registration rules the guidance did not mention.
Anybody whose safety depends on that needs a specialist and a lawyer, not a checklist. Saying otherwise is the failure mode of this entire topic.
Use a second device for compartmentalisation, which is what almost everybody reading this actually needs.
Do not confuse that with anonymity, and do not let a lesson convince you that you have achieved anonymity because you paid cash.
The gap between those two things is where people get hurt, and it is exactly the gap this kind of material tends to blur.
